rss.title: Building without predicting
rss.content_excerpt: On a podcast , I briefly mentioned that I’m building my dream house without predicting - by living in a bare cabin in the woods, then adding only what I find I actually need . Apparently it was intriguing, because since then, it’s been my most frequently asked question: “How’s your house going?” I didn’t think this would interest total strangers, but enough people have asked, so here’s the story. rss.title: Pushing 4.7M Commits an Hour
rss.author: matt@mattrickard.com (Matt Rickard)
rss.content_excerpt: The winning software teams will throw away orders of magnitude more code than they merge. I ran a benchmark against the custom git server I’m building, 4.79 million pushes per hour to a single repository across 1,408 branches (p50, 322ms). 27.8 million clones per hour of a repository containing the NextJS starter template (p50, 220ms). 4.79M commits won’t make it to master, but the frontier labs are running that many experiments at scale, and the rest of us will be soon.
